basis: Herniation of intracranial contents through a congenital parietal skull defect defines both neural and skeletal abnormalities.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: the congenital parietal bone defect is an essential anatomical component of the encephalocele.

basis: Bilateral cerebral cortical malformation; esotropia occurs in 30-79% but does not establish direct ocular injury or visual loss. Hearing impairment occurs in 5-29%.

decisions.ocular: none: frequent esotropia reflects ocular alignment dysfunction; direct eye damage or loss of vision is not established.

basis: Purine metabolic disorder defined by developmental impairment and seizures; strabismus in 4/7 patients does not establish direct ocular damage or visual loss.

decisions.ocular: none: strabismus affects 4/7 patients, but misalignment alone does not demonstrate direct ocular damage or visual loss.

basis: Hepatitis, osteochondritis/periostitis and infection-related anemia each affect roughly 30-60% of symptomatic early cases. Transient rash excluded; persistent CNS injury less consistently common.

decisions.haematologic: involved: infection-related hemolysis and marrow dysfunction cause anemia in roughly 30-60% of symptomatic early cases.

basis: Endocrine dysfunction, intellectual disability and sensorineural deafness define the syndrome. Alopecia is another defining feature in the four-sibling report; primary limited to three axes.

decisions.dermatologic: involved: alopecia is a defining manifestation of the reported syndrome; the three primary slots prioritize endocrine, cognitive and hearing impairment.
decisions.otologic: primary: sensorineural deafness is a defining neuroectodermal abnormality.

basis: Defining severe CNS impairment; heart defects ~80%, ocular malformations ~50-70%, oral clefts ~60%. Common polydactyly/limb anomalies omitted at cap because generally less damaging.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: congenital heart defects occur in approximately 80% and directly impair cardiac structure and function.
decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: cleft lip/palate occurs in approximately 60%, directly affecting oral structure and feeding function.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: common polydactyly and limb anomalies qualify anatomically but are generally less damaging than the four retained axes; omitted at cap.

basis: Bacterial infection with massive adrenal hemorrhage, adrenal insufficiency and defining DIC. Circulatory shock alone does not establish direct cardiac or vascular injury.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: shock reflects sepsis and adrenal failure; separate direct cardiac or vascular injury is not established by the syndrome.

basis: Spotted-fever rickettsiae infect vascular endothelium and cause small-vessel vasculitis. The transient exanthem does not establish additional skin damage.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: vascular endothelium is the principal infected tissue, with direct small-vessel inflammation characteristic of spotted-fever rickettsiosis.

basis: Inflammation directly affects glanular and preputial skin. Infectious, irritant and other causes occur, so the umbrella does not establish an infectious or autoimmune mechanism.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: balanoposthitis directly inflames external genital skin, including the foreskin; this supplies a dermatologic axis despite the reproductive location.

basis: IgG4-mediated retroperitoneal fibrosis; ureteral encasement with hydronephrosis/renal impairment and large-vessel vasculitis each occur in 30-79%. Secondary anemia does not show direct blood injury.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: large-vessel vasculitis occurs in 30-79%; fibrosis surrounding vessels alone does not make the disorder primarily vascular.
